user_consequence: A WKWebView URL that happens to contain the substring "/golf/" anywhere (not anchored to path start, no origin/host check) is treated as a legitimate in-app page and the native safety net that returns the user to the sign-in screen never fires. Conversely a genuine in-app URL that omits that exact substring (e.g. the bare "/golf" root before its server redirect resolves) can misfire the callback, which reloads the WKWebView with a full hardcoded document navigation to https://www.helmsportslabs.com/golf/login, discarding all SPA state including any unsaved round/session data with no confirmation.
mechanism: GolfBridgeViewController.swift observes webView.url via KVO and classifies navigation with two unanchored String.contains checks (no origin/scheme comparison, no path-prefix anchoring): isGolfPage = url.contains("/golf/"); isAboutPage = url.contains("/about")||contains("/privacy")||contains("/terms"). When neither matches, SceneDelegate's onNavigateAway closure fires a hardcoded webView.load(URLRequest(url: "https://www.helmsportslabs.com/golf/login")) - a full document reload, not an SPA route change.
expected: Navigation classification should anchor on the app's actual origin/host and path prefix (e.g. URL host equals the deployed app host AND path starts with /golf/), not a bare substring match anywhere in the URL string; a false classification either way should not cause a silent security bypass or an undiscovered destructive reload of in-progress work.
actual: Classification is two unanchored String.contains calls with no host/origin check at all.
proposed_fix: A01 (native shell owner) anchors the classifier on URL.host matching the deployed app host and URL.path having the /golf/ (or /about, /privacy, /terms) prefix, using URLComponents rather than raw string containment. A08 requests this as a shared contract (C05 viewport/native boundary) since the failure mode intersects auth/session integrity.

user_consequence: An OAuth/magic-link sign-in that hits a transient golf_coaches/golf_players read failure can momentarily route an ALREADY-onboarded coach or player into first-run onboarding UI instead of the dashboard. Both onboarding pages independently self-correct (they re-check onboarding_completed on mount and redirect to /golf/dashboard), so the user does not get stuck or lose data, but they see a flash of the wrong first-run screen and pay an extra round trip - exactly the 'returning users repeat onboarding' failure the plan calls out, even though the fix elsewhere in this codebase (join/[code]/page.tsx) explicitly treats a failed identity read as fail-closed rather than fail-as-new-user.
mechanism: src/app/auth/callback/route.ts destructures only `data` from three `.single()` reads (golf_coaches, golf_players at lines 197-200; baseball_coaches/baseball_players at 231-234) and never inspects the accompanying `error`. A genuine transient read failure produces the same `{data: null}` shape as 'row does not exist', so the callback's `if (golfCoach)` / `if (golfPlayer)` checks cannot distinguish the two and fall through to 'No golf profile exists - redirect to golf signup' (line 224-227) for an existing, onboarded user.
expected: A failed profile read during OAuth callback routing should be distinguished from 'no profile exists' (same pattern already applied in src/app/golf/join/[code]/page.tsx:38-53, 100-106), and should not silently misroute an established user through onboarding UI.
actual: Read errors for golf_coaches/golf_players (and the baseball equivalents) are discarded; only the sibling join/[code] route was fixed for this class of bug.
proposed_fix: Check `error` on each `.single()`/read in the callback route and, on a failed (not merely empty) read, show a retry/error state or fall back to a safe default (e.g. dashboard, which itself re-verifies) rather than assuming 'no profile'. Low-risk, isolated to route.ts.

user_consequence: Tapping Sign out anywhere in the golf app (rail footer, More sheet, Settings) fires immediately with no confirmation and no check for in-progress local work, even though the app maintains a real offline round-draft store (IndexedDB, scoped by playerId) with its own recovery UI. A player who signs out (or is signed out by someone else on a shared device) mid-round gets no warning that unsynced local progress exists, contradicting the plan's explicit 'warn before logout when possible, then enforce the confirmed security policy' requirement. The app already has this exact UX pattern built (a 'Discard unsaved changes?' ConfirmDialog) for Settings-panel edits, just not applied to sign-out or to round drafts.
mechanism: useGolfSignOut() in FairwayDashboardShell.tsx and handleSignOut in FairwaySettingsGeneral.tsx both call clearActiveTeam() + supabase.auth.signOut() unconditionally on click, with only a `isSigningOut` double-tap guard - no query against src/lib/offline/indexed-db.ts / shot-storage.ts for a recoverable round, and no reuse of the ConfirmDialog leave-guard pattern already present in the same settings file (lines 163-275) for its own dirty-panel tracking.
expected: Sign-out should check for a recoverable in-progress round for the current playerId (the same query FairwayRecoverRound.tsx already performs) and warn the user before proceeding, consistent with the leave-guard pattern already implemented for Settings edits.
actual: No such check exists at any sign-out call site; sign-out is unconditional once tapped.
proposed_fix: Share a 'hasRecoverableRoundProgress(playerId)' check (reusing FairwayRecoverRound's existing query) behind the sign-out handlers, and gate on a ConfirmDialog ('You have an unsynced round - sign out anyway?') mirroring the pattern already in FairwaySettingsGeneral.tsx:163-275. Cross-lane: the offline round store is A05's domain; A08 requests the read-only check as a shared utility rather than owning it.

user_consequence: An established, already-onboarded golf coach or player who hits two consecutive transient DB read failures (roughly 300ms apart) while loading any dashboard page is redirected to /golf/signup, /golf/coach, or /golf/player as if they had never created a profile - the single highest-traffic auth gate in the golf app (used by 40+ routes via getGolfSessionProfile) cannot distinguish 'no profile' from 'failed to read profile' in this narrow window.
mechanism: getGolfSessionProfile() in session.ts destructures only `.data` from the golf_coaches/golf_players reads (never `.error`). The dashboard layout's own mitigation (a direct re-query when neither profile shows onboarding_completed, layout.tsx:101-119) is a real, well-designed retry that catches most transient blips, but it too only checks `retryCoachResult.data`/`retryPlayerResult.data` and never `retryCoachResult.error`/`retryPlayerResult.error` - so if BOTH the original cached call and the ~300ms-later retry fail (not merely return zero rows), the user still falls through to the 'Unknown state - redirect to onboarding' branch at layout.tsx:276-283.
expected: A read failure (vs. a genuine empty result) for the coach/player profile lookup should not be treated as equivalent to 'no profile exists' at the app's central dashboard gate.
actual: Both the primary cached lookup and its own retry discard read errors, silently treating them as absence.
proposed_fix: Thread the `error` from both golf_coaches/golf_players reads through GolfSessionProfile (or a sibling field), and have the dashboard layout show a retry/error state instead of redirecting to onboarding when the reads themselves failed rather than returned empty.

user_consequence: The exact same team join code produces two different outcomes depending only on which UI surface the player uses to redeem it: opening the deep-link /golf/join/[code] auto-joins the team immediately with no coach involvement, while typing the identical code into Settings' 'Request to Join a Team' form creates a pending request that requires the coach to approve it. A coach who believes every new roster addition goes through their approval (the entire reason the request/approval feature exists) may not realize that sharing the code as a clickable link bypasses that review entirely.
mechanism: Both entry points resolve the same golf_teams.join_code via the same golf_team_by_join_code RPC. processGolfTeamInvitationImpl (teams.ts:551-587) calls joinGolfTeamImpl, which inserts directly into golf_team_members via golf_join_team_with_code (teams.ts:429-437) with no approval step. createTeamJoinRequestImpl (teams.ts:908 onward) resolves the identical code but inserts into golf_team_join_requests as status 'pending' instead, requiring separate coach approval.
expected: Either both entry points should require the same approval posture for a given team's configured join policy, or the difference should be an intentional, coach-visible setting (e.g. 'require approval for link joins too') rather than an implicit consequence of which screen redeemed the code.
actual: No visible product setting distinguishes the two; the difference is purely a function of code path.
proposed_fix: Open question for the product owner: confirm whether auto-join-via-link is an intentional convenience (the coach who mints/shares the link is presumed to have already vetted recipients) or an oversight that should require the same approval gate as the Settings entry form.
